chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Three months in Hartford Hospital and his wife's fight to get home to the baby
summary: Cobb woke in traction; his wife, who had lost earlier pregnancies, fought to recover and went home with a broken arm to care for baby Lisette.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Really, I was numb. And I don't know what they did. They took me to the hospital and they knocked me out, and they had to cut my clothes off. They cut my trousers off because they couldn't get them off, to set my leg. And I don't know nothing after that. When I woke up I was in a bed with pinions in me, weights on me, and in a strange territory, and they had -- standing in the back where you reach up to pull yourself up and all that. I was just -- I didn't know where I was.
How long were you out, do you reckon?
I imagine overnight because I remember waking up until the next morning.
You must have been out a long time.
Yeah, it was a long time.
Were you in a Hartford hospital?

Hartford Hospital. I stayed in there three months. My wife had a broken arm, and they let her out before me because she was determined to get out and go home and take care of her baby because she was just yelling and she wanted to get to her that baby.

And they let both of us see the baby in the hospital before they let her left out with my mother (inaudible) and that was something unusual for usually a young baby like that, but my wife didn't have a desire to live if her baby was dead, because we had lost four prior or five to her. She was anemic. She could conceive but couldn't hold. And if that baby didn't live, she knew this baby three months and 12 days, she had no desire to live. But when she saw that Lizette, she fought. She fought.
And then she was determined -- she went home in a swing to take care of that baby with one arm, and she did it. She left before me.
No, we were living in Englewood, New Jersey, Englewood, New Jersey. But Lisette was born in New York at [Sinai] Hospital.
